newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Nov. 18, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - In an effort to keep Java from splintering into incompatible camps, JavaSoft is pulling together a strategy to turn the Internet language over to standards bodies, which will begin in the next few months and take 18 months to two years to complete, PC Week reported Nov. 18.

The IT community is cautiously optimisitic about the new handheld devices based on Microsoft Corp's new CE operating system, as they remember the promise of such devices when the Apple Computer Inc Newton was unveiled in 1993, PC Week reported Nov. 18.

COMPUTERWORLD - Despite a powerful push by Sun Microsystems Inc, Oracle Corp and IBM Corp of the low-cost network computers, information systems managers at large companies are viewing NCs mainly for niche uses, not for PC replacement, Computerworld reported Nov. 17.
The arrival of the network computer may trigger changes that favor users in sotware pricing and licensing by simplifying licensing and lowering the cost of software, Computerworld reported Nov. 17.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - Despite concerns the technology could add to existing strain on the Internet, many large companies are gearing up to take advantage of fax delivery systems that transmit documents via the Internet instead of convential phone networks, eliminating long distance charges, Communications Week reported in its November 18 issue.
U S West Communications Group is gearing up to expand its high speed communications network capacity and plans to offer low-cost data services in 300 cities by the end of 1997, CW also reported.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp will delay the release of Internet Explorer 4.0 until the middle of 1997, nearly a year after the release of IE 3.0, in order to incorporate its new Trident software, CRN reported Nov. 17.

Hewlett-Packard Co which has been a no-show at the Internet party, is about to make a splash with a comprehensive Internet strategy across both its UNIX and NT platforms, CRN said in its Nov. 17 issue.

INFOWORLD - Netscape Communications Corp will unveil enhancements to its Communicator software this week that will position the software as the primary interface for accessing desktop applications, aiming at replacing Microsoft Corp's Windows user interface, Infoworld reported Nov. 18.

At this week's Comdex show in Las Vegas, a large number of portable vendors will be displaying notebooks with big screens of 13.3 inches and even 14 inches, anticipated for the first and second quarters of next year, Infoworld reported Nov. 17.

INFORMATION WEEK - Borland International Inc's Delphi 97 has entered beta testing and is drawing rave reviews, but potential customers are concerned about Borland's recent financial weakness, Information Week reported Nov. 18.
American Telephone and Telegraph Co is rolling out three services aimed at managing data networks for customers, Information Week reported.
ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - The European Union and the European chip industry continue to balk at U.S. demands to eliminate semiconductor tariffs in 1997, EBN reported Nov. 18.

Intel Corp is gearing up to place all of its new processors for notebook computers in special modules starting next year, a strategy that will allow the machines to be equipped with its fastest - and most profitable - chips.
Intel Corp rolled out its new motherboard standard last week, setting the stage for its new Klamath processor, EBN reported Nov. 18.

COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - As the first five handheld products based on Microsoft Corp's Windows CE software debut at Comdex this week, Microsoft predicted that a plethora of other products, ranging from smart phones to entertainment devices, will be developed for future versions of Windows CE, Computer Retail Week reported Nov. 18.

Two market research firms have handed the current market share crown of the home/retail PC market to Compaq Computer Corp, which has gained share from Packard Bell NEC, according to Computer Intelligence and PC Data, but two other firms dispute those results and said Packard Bell still leads, Computer Retail Week reported Nov. 18.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - The digital set-top box may be going nowhere in the U.S., but it's become the focus of a massive design effort across the Atlantic in Europe, with European broadcasters and global content providers gearing up to leverage the EC's planned 1998 deregulation of the telcom industry, EE Times reported Nov. 18.

INTERACTIVE WEEK - AT&T Corp's electronic mail service in its WorldNet service went down again on November 13 and November 14, barely a week after a brownout of 31 hours, Interactive Week reported Nov. 18.

A proposal before the ad-hoc international body that reviews the procedures for registering Internet addresses could divide domain names into two classes, such as "vanity names" such as ibm.org, which would sell for significant sums of money. The other names, random names such as f4k.vcf9, would be handed out for nominal fees, which would freeze out the use of plain English domain names for individual users.
